archetype.name: Pocket Passer (vertical)
archetype.definition: A rhythm-and-timing thrower who works from the pocket and takes his shots downfield, living with long dropbacks that turn into sacks when nothing comes open.

report.headline: Better than 1-4 says: a cleaner, deeper Stroud undone by sacks and stalled third downs
report.take:
Stroud is still the quarterback he has been since 2023: he hangs in the pocket close to three seconds (2.96 this year, against 3.04, 2.98 and 2.82 in his first three seasons), reads the field and throws with timing rather than off-script. What has changed is intent. His aggressiveness is 20%, well above the 12.8-15.4% range of every prior season, and intended air yards are up to 10.06 from a career aDOT of 8-9.2. The extra risk is paying. He is +0.447 EPA on 30 deep attempts and +0.343 on intermediate throws, and he has done it without a single interception or a single interception-worthy throw.

So why is he 20th in EPA per dropback and the team 1-4? The damage happens in a few specific spots. Third down is a hole: -0.163 EPA, a 31.4% conversion rate and 7 of his 14 sacks on 51 plays, with the average third down at 8.6 yards to go. Long-yardage downs are what a run game ranked 26th in EPA produces, and they are where his habit of holding the ball costs the most. The screen game is dead weight too: 19 throws behind the line, -0.451 EPA. Add two lost fumbles in the opener and a 55-attempt, -6.4 EPA dud against Cincinnati, and a strong passing profile turns into a mediocre composite.

The 4th-ranked passing yardage overstates him a little. He is throwing 37 times a game, and 353 of those yards came in the Cincinnati loss, where they were worth nothing. The 34th-ranked TD rate understates him: he has 5 touchdowns on 20 red-zone attempts, and the problem is drives that die on third down before they get there.

The trajectory is good. The last two games were his best, +15.2 and +10.5 passing EPA with CPOE of 15.1 and 10.0. Nico Collins is quietly the most efficient target he has, at 0.755 EPA on only 25 targets. If the offense funnels more volume his way and the run game stops leaving him in third-and-long, the efficiency should start turning into points.

strengths.title: Downfield aggression without the turnovers
strengths.body: He is pushing the ball more than at any point in his career, and the intermediate and deep throws are his most valuable plays. The 0 interceptions come with 0 interception-worthy throws and a bad-throw rate (13%) that is cleaner than any prior season, so this looks like better decisions, not luck. Some interceptions will come with volume, but the decision-making change looks real.

strengths.title: Accuracy above expectation
strengths.body: His tracked CPOE of 6.73 is a big step up from a career that hovered around zero, including -1.7 in 2024. The short game is efficient at 78.2% and +0.288 EPA, and he has been at his best late in close games (+15.1 CPOE in fourth-quarter one-score situations). Five games is a modest sample, but the last two weeks moved this the right way rather than inflating one fluke game.

strengths.title: Collins and Noel as efficiency engines
strengths.body: Collins (0.755 EPA per target) and Jaylin Noel (0.631) are producing far more per look than the two most-targeted players, Schultz and Hutchinson. The volume has been spread toward the less efficient options. That is a play-calling and distribution lever with room to grow, not a ceiling on Stroud.

concerns.title: Sacks from holding the ball
concerns.body: He is pressured on only 20.3% of dropbacks, a middle-of-the-pack rate, yet 30% of those pressures become sacks. That is the price of his style: he waits for routes to develop instead of escaping or throwing it away. It is not new. 2023 (30.9%) and 2024 (29.9%) looked the same, which makes 2025's 22.1% the outlier, so expect this to persist.

concerns.title: Third-and-long is killing drives
concerns.body: Half his sacks have come on third down, where Houston averages 8.6 yards to go and converts under a third of the time. The root cause is upstream: a run game 26th in EPA, now likely without David Montgomery (doubtful, groin), keeps putting him behind the sticks. That will not fix itself soon, so his TD rate stays capped until early downs improve.

concerns.title: Ball security in the pocket
concerns.body: He has three turnover-worthy fumbles and two lost, both in Week 1, which goes with taking 14 sacks and absorbing hits on 14.9% of dropbacks. The lost-fumble count will likely cool, but the exposure stays as long as the sack rate does.

trend.note: He opened with two mixed games, including a hollow 353 yards in a -6.4 EPA loss to Cincinnati, then bottomed out at Indianapolis. Weeks 4-5 were his two best games, +15.2 and +10.5 passing EPA with double-digit CPOE.

nextGame.headline: Pass-funnel Jacksonville invites volume but takes away the easy stuff
nextGame.body:
Jacksonville is the third-best defense by EPA and the stingiest in the league on short throws (-0.334). That hits the part of Stroud's game built on checkdowns and screens. The run defense is also third, and offenses pass on it 5.8 points more than normal, the fourth-strongest pass funnel. With Houston's ground game already 26th, expect another heavy-attempt afternoon. The openings are vertical: Jacksonville is 23rd against deep passes, gives up the 29th-most passing yards to quarterbacks, and gets home on only 5.6% of dropbacks (19th), which helps a quarterback who holds the ball. The catch is touchdowns. It allows one per game to quarterbacks, second-fewest, so this sets up as yards between the 20s more than scoring.

Availability favors the deep game. Starting safety Eric Murray (76% of snaps) is out with a concussion, and corner Montaric Brown (53%) is questionable with a hamstring, which thins the back end Stroud wants to attack. On Houston's side, Montgomery being doubtful pushes even more of the offense onto Stroud, and Braden Smith's IR stint changes nothing, since he hasn't played this season. Jacksonville right tackle Anton Harrison (92% of snaps, questionable, knee) matters for Houston's third-ranked sack defense. The early forecast shows 14 mph wind with gusts near 28 in an outdoor stadium; if that holds it would hurt the deep shots, but it is five days out and shouldn't be over-weighted yet.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots versus a thinned secondary
keyMatchups.body: His most valuable throws are 20+ yards downfield, and that is Jacksonville's soft spot, now without Murray. Collins, Jacksonville's likely WR1 assignment, has been held 4.7 PPR under average by role yet allowed 0.52 EPA per target. The windows exist if Stroud takes them.

keyMatchups.title: Short game into the league's best wall
keyMatchups.body: Jacksonville allows -0.334 EPA on short passes, the best mark in the league. Houston's screens (-0.451 behind the line) and quick game are likely to stall, which means more third-and-longs, where Stroud's sacks pile up.

keyMatchups.title: Pass funnel forces volume
keyMatchups.body: A top-three run defense against a bottom-seven run offense missing its lead back points Houston toward 35+ dropbacks. Jacksonville's modest sack rate means more of those dropbacks become actual throws.

nextGame.watch: Whether Houston feeds Collins downfield against a secondary missing Murray, or keeps throwing short into the league's best short-pass defense.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation looks sustainable. The aggression with clean decision-making, the CPOE gain and the deep efficiency have all held or improved over the season, and Houston's run game is weak enough to keep his attempts high. Expect yardage to stay strong, though in a more efficient offense it will come on somewhat fewer than 37 attempts a game. The TD rate (3.2%) should drift upward if the last two weeks are closer to the real level, since red-zone conversion has not been the problem.

What will not change is the sack habit. It has defined three of his four seasons, and as long as early downs keep failing, third downs will cost drives. The zero-interception run will end at some point with this many deep throws, but the underlying charting suggests he stays among the lower-turnover passers. The ceiling depends on targets: more of the offense flowing through Collins and Noel is the clearest path from good efficiency to good scoring.
swingFactors: Whether the run game (and Montgomery's return) stops creating third-and-long
Target share shifting toward Collins and Noel

bets.reason: Jacksonville is a strong pass funnel with a top-three run defense, Montgomery is doubtful, and the defense gives up the 29th-most passing yards to quarterbacks while missing its starting safety. The early wind forecast is the main risk.
Jacksonville allows one passing TD per game to quarterbacks, second-fewest, and Houston's third-down struggles (31.4% conversion) keep drives from reaching the red zone.

Jacksonville's defense ranks third in EPA and Houston's ranks fourth in success rate. Houston's offense is likely to be stuck in long-yardage passing downs without a run game, and the early forecast shows gusty wind.

confidence.note: Five games, but the core passing traits line up with his career; the shift in aggression is new and still small-sample.
